label: Rank 9 CONFIRMED repo-wide: of 45 files matching CODE_QUALITY_RESULT or code-quality/v1, the only executable hits are the producer, one presence guard and a scratch copy of that guard; no parser or consumer exists, and the .claude, .opencode and .codex trees returned no hit.

A second producer copy of the envelope block exists at .hermes/skills/sk-code-quality/SKILL.md:215-216; it emits the same schema id and parses nothing, so it is a duplicate producer, not the missing consumer.

Rank 10's 'HOOK_FLAGS_CONFIG is the only settings seam' is REFUTED: check-dist-staleness.sh reads three environment keys - HOOK_FLAGS_CONFIG at line 31, a generic SYSTEM_*_DISABLED per-process override at line 63, and SPECKIT_DIST_AUTO_REBUILD at line 136.
The load-bearing half of rank 10 survives: no seam in the quality packet configures checklists or label patterns, and HOOK_FLAGS_CONFIG only resolves hooks/hook-flags.env hook-enable flags.
Rank 10's 'the label patterns are a literal list' is CONFIRMED: ALLOWED_PATTERNS and VIOLATION_PATTERNS are module-level list literals, and the comment checker reads no environment at all.

External-User Modes row-4 claim CONFIRMED: row 4 is the stage-two INTENT_SIGNALS plus RESOURCE_MAP row, its failure mode is 'The mode is selected but loads no leaves', and the reference lists rows 4, 5, 6, 8 and 10 as having no gate.
Section 8 row 1 CONFIRMED: the always-loaded checklist describes itself as a JavaScript and CSS checklist, so it cannot be copied wholesale as a portable core.
Section 8 row 8 CONFIRMED: quality's target-path checklist map remains authoritative on current disk, so a registered or bundled surface is not proof that quality loads its checklist.

Internal contradiction in the synthesis: rank 10's justification says HOOK_FLAGS_CONFIG is the only settings seam while rank 14 depends on SPECKIT_DIST_AUTO_REBUILD as a second environment seam; the justification needs the narrower claim that no seam configures checklists or label patterns.
